diagnosis.original_evidence: The existing R64 hook installs ID3DXSprite::Begin/Draw/Flush/End slots 8-11 and retains thread-local tracked Begin/Draw/StageBoundaryReady across calls. ID3DXSprite::OnLostDevice/OnResetDevice at slots 12-13 had no hooks or state reset.
source_trace: Exact +TIME six E8 producers enter direct or queued stage scope.
R64 Begin/Draw tracks per-batch scope and may defer actual GPU Flush/End.
D3DXSprite device-loss/reset can invalidate its internal GPU batch without invoking R64 End, after which a stale pending owner can be reused.
diagnosis.root_cause: No lifecycle invalidation existed for the thread-local R64 deferred batch tracker when D3DXSprite internal GPU resources were discarded and reconstructed.
alternatives_rejected: Do not globally force Flush on device loss or every D3DX draw; that would change unrelated alpha order and misattribute old sprites.
Do not assume static source evidence proves the actual game stage +TIME binocular defect is fixed.
Do not modify or replace DXVK or shared DX11 host renderer.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: The original D3DX methods still run and return their HRESULT; only exact game sprite callbacks clear BatchActive, StageBoundaryReady, PendingDraws, PendingScope, PendingProducer and TrackedSprite.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Active R64 source/mutation verifier checks both lifecycle slot callbacks, trampoline rollback, exact sprite predicate, stale pointer reset, missed invalidation, and legacy stage/GOAL ownership.
diagnosis.eye_ownership: Avoids stale producer-driven R26+HUD per-eye selection after a D3D9 device generation change; does not demonstrate that the original +TIME sprite and numeric images converge visually in Quest3.

runtime_evidence: No original game or Quest3/VDXR HMD execution in this dispatch; no runtime PASS or lens/+TIME optical fix claim.
